step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows PwC's supply chain solution. SAP ERP initiates purchase orders via API calls into Amazon Managed Blockchain (running Hyperledger Fabric 1.2). AWS IoT Core captures physical asset telemetry (location, movement thresholds) and writes updates to the blockchain ledger. In return, the blockchain sends status updates and notifications back to IoT Core and SAP. Generic user icons at the top are pruned as non-runtime actors per the node rules.

graph.name: PwC Blockchain Supply Chain Architecture
graph.notes: PwC blockchain-powered supply chain solution leveraging Amazon Managed Blockchain, SAP ERP integration, and AWS IoT Core telemetry.

nodes.name: SAP ERP
nodes.notes: Enterprise Resource Planning system where purchase orders originate and integrate via API calls.

nodes.name: Amazon Managed Blockchain
nodes.notes: Central immutable ledger running Hyperledger Fabric 1.2 to maintain end-to-end transparency, privacy, and smart contract chaincode execution.

nodes.name: AWS IoT Core
nodes.notes: Collects real-time telemetry, location, and movement threshold data from physical supply chain assets.

edges.notes: SAP sends purchase order data into Amazon Managed Blockchain via API call.
Amazon Managed Blockchain updates SAP with reconciled single source of truth ledger state.
AWS IoT Core sends asset location and telemetry threshold data to Amazon Managed Blockchain.
Amazon Managed Blockchain triggers notifications and state updates back via IoT Core when rule breaches occur.
